DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y \
  build-essential cmake git wget curl unzip python3 python3-pip python3-venv \
  libncurses-dev libtinfo-dev zlib1g-dev libz3-dev \

DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y \
  build-essential cmake git wget curl unzip python3 python3-pip python3-venv \
  libncurses-dev libtinfo-dev zlib1g-dev libz3-dev \
  clang llvm llvm-dev lld liblld-dev \
  libsqlite3-dev libgmp-dev \
  bison flex pkg-config \

while fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done; echo "Lock released"; dpkg --configure -a 2>&1 | tail -5
ps aux | grep -E 'apt|dpkg|218' | grep -v grep; echo "---"; kill -9 218 2>/dev/null; sleep 5; while fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done; echo "Lock released"
while fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 3; done; echo "Lock released"; dpkg --configure -a 2>&1 | tail -5; echo "=== dpkg configured ==="

echo "Checking what got installed:"; dpkg -l | grep -E 'build-essential|cmake|git|clang|llvm|libz3|libsqlite3|libgmp|bison|flex|autoconf|automake|libtool|libcap|libssl-dev|graphviz' | head -40; echo "=== LLVM version ==="; llvm-config --version 2>/dev/null || echo "not found"; clang --version 2>/dev/null | head -1 || echo "clang not found"

cd /workspace && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/klee/klee.git 2>&1 | tail -5; echo "=== KLEE cloned ==="; git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/radareorg/radare2.git 2>&1 | tail -5; echo "=== radare2 cloned ==="

cd /workspace/klee && cat README.md | head -100; echo "=== CMake requirements ==="; grep -i "llvm" CMakeLists.txt | head -20; echo "=== Required LLVM versions ==="; grep -i "LLVM_VERSION" CMakeLists.txt | head -10

cd /workspace/klee && grep -i "LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR" CMakeLists.txt | head -20; echo "=== max version check ==="; grep -i "GREATER" CMakeLists.txt | grep -i llvm | head -10; echo "=== solvers ==="; grep -i "stp\|z3\|solver" CMakeLists.txt | head -20
cd /workspace/klee && cat cmake/find_z3.cmake | head -40

cd /workspace/klee && mkdir -p build && cd build && cmake \
  -DENABLE_SOLVER_Z3=ON \
  -DENABLE_SOLVER_STP=OFF \
  -DENABLE_SOLVER_METASMT=OFF \
  -DENABLE_KLEE_UCLIBC=OFF \
  -DENABLE_KLEE_LIBCXX=OFF \
  -DENABLE_POSIX_RUNTIME=OFF \
  -DENABLE_UNIT_TESTS=OFF \
  -DENABLE_SYSTEM_TESTS=OFF \
  -DLLVM_DIR=$(llvm-config --cmakedir) \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  .. 2>&1 | tail -40
DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y libgoogle-perftools-dev libtcmalloc-minimal4 libffi-dev libedit-dev 2>&1 | tail -10

cd /workspace/klee && rm -rf build && mkdir -p build && cd build && cmake \
  -DENABLE_SOLVER_Z3=ON \
  -DENABLE_SOLVER_STP=OFF \
  -DENABLE_SOLVER_METASMT=OFF \
  -DENABLE_KLEE_UCLIBC=OFF \
  -DENABLE_KLEE_LIBCXX=OFF \
  -DENABLE_POSIX_RUNTIME=OFF \
  -DENABLE_UNIT_TESTS=OFF \
  -DENABLE_SYSTEM_TESTS=OFF \
  -DLLVM_DIR=$(llvm-config --cmakedir) \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  .. 2>&1 | tail -40
cd /workspace/klee/build && make -j$(nproc) 2>&1 | tail -30
cd /workspace/klee/build && ls -la bin/; echo "=== klee version ==="; ./bin/klee --version 2>&1 | head -10; echo "=== which tools ==="; ls bin/

cd /workspace/radare2 && ls -la; echo "=== subdirs ==="; find . -maxdepth 2 -type d | head -40; echo "=== Makefile ==="; head -50 Makefile 2>/dev/null || echo "no Makefile"; echo "=== configure ==="; ls configure* 2>/dev/null || echo "no configure"; echo "=== meson ==="; ls meson.build 2>/dev/null || echo "no meson"
cd /workspace/radare2 && ls libr/; echo "=== struct of libr ==="; find libr -maxdepth 2 -type d | head -30; echo "=== find simple standalone C files ==="; find libr -name "*.c" | head -20
cd /workspace/radare2 && find libr -name "*.c" | wc -l; echo "=== small standalone files ==="; find libr/util -name "*.c" | xargs wc -l 2>/dev/null | sort -n | head -20
cd /workspace/radare2 && cat libr/util/base36.c; echo "=== queue ==="; cat libr/util/queue.c

cd /workspace/radare2 && head -60 libr/include/r_util.h 2>/dev/null | head -60; echo "=== queue header ==="; find libr -name "queue.h" -o -name "*queue*" | head -10; cat libr/include/r_util/r_queue.h 2>/dev/null || find . -name "r_queue.h" -exec cat {} \; 2>/dev/null | head -50
cd /workspace/radare2 && head -100 libr/include/r_types.h; echo "=== R_API macro ==="; grep -n "R_API\|R_NEW0\|R_NEWS0\|ut64\|ut32\|ut8" libr/include/r_types.h | head -30

cd /workspace/radare2 && grep -n "typedef.*ut64\|typedef.*ut32\|typedef.*ut8\|typedef.*ut16\|#define ut64\|#define ut32\|#define ut8\|#define R_NEW0\|#define R_NEWS0\|r_new0" libr/include/r_types_base.h | head -20; echo "=== r_userconf ==="; find . -name "r_userconf.h" | head -5; cat libr/include/r_userconf.h 2>/dev/null | head -20 || echo "not found"

cd /workspace/radare2 && find . -name "r_userconf.h*" -o -name "userconf.h" | head -10; echo "=== check if it needs to be generated ==="; grep "r_userconf" libr/include/r_types.h; echo "=== configure for headers ==="; head -30 configure.acr | grep -i userconf
cd /workspace/radare2 && cat libr/include/r_userconf.h.acr; echo "=== r_types_base.h ut16 ==="; grep "ut16" libr/include/r_types_base.h | head -5
cd /workspace/radare2 && ./configure --prefix=/opt/radare2 2>&1 | tail -30

cd /workspace/radare2 && head -20 libr/include/r_userconf.h; echo "=== R_API ==="; grep -n "^#define R_API" libr/include/r_types.h; grep -n "R_NEW0\b" libr/include/r_types.h; grep -n "r_new0\|R_NEW0\|R_NEWS0" libr/include/r_types.h | head -10; echo "=== r_types_null.h ==="; cat libr/include/r_types_null.h | head -20
cd /workspace/radare2 && sed -n '355,380p' libr/include/r_types.h

cd /workspace/radare2 && clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I libr/include \
  libr/util/queue.c -o /tmp/queue.bc 2>&1 | head -30
cd /workspace/radare2 && find . -name "r_version.h" | head -5; echo "=== generated? ==="; ls -la libr/include/r_version.h 2>/dev/null || echo "not found - need to generate"

cd /workspace/radare2 && grep -r "r_version.h" Makefile global.mk configure.acr 2>/dev/null | head -10; echo "=== search generation ==="; find . -name "r_version.h*" | head -5; grep -r "r_version" mk/ 2>/dev/null | head -10
cd /workspace/radare2 && cat libr/include/r_version.h.in; echo "=== Makefile rule ==="; grep -A 20 "libr/include/r_version.h:" Makefile

cd /workspace/radare2 && cat > libr/include/r_version.h << 'EOF'
#ifndef R_VERSION_H
#define R_VERSION_H 1
#define R_MESON_VERSION ""
#define R2_VERSION_MAJOR 6
#define R2_VERSION_MINOR 1
#define R2_VERSION_PATCH 9
#define R2_VERSION_NUMBER 60109
#define R2_VERSION_COMMIT 0
#define R2_VERSION "6.1.9"
#define R2_GITTAP "6.1.9"
#define R2_GITTIP ""
#define R2_BIRTH ""
#define R2_ABIVERSION_STRING "6.1.9"
#endif
EOF
echo "r_version.h created"; ls -la libr/include/r_version.h

cd /workspace/radare2 && clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I libr/include \
  libr/util/queue.c -o /tmp/queue.bc 2>&1 | head -30
cd /workspace/radare2 && find . -name "sdb.h" | head -5; echo "=== shlr ==="; ls shlr/; echo "=== sdb dir ==="; ls shlr/sdb/ 2>/dev/null | head -10
cd /workspace/radare2 && cat shlr/sdb.mk | head -30; echo "=== sdb submodule? ==="; cat .gitmodules 2>/dev/null | head -30; find . -path "*/sdb/src/sdb.h" | head -5
cd /workspace/radare2 && ls subprojects/; echo "=== sdb in subprojects ==="; ls subprojects/sdb/ 2>/dev/null | head -10; find subprojects -name "sdb.h" | head -5
cd /workspace/radare2 && cat subprojects/sdb.wrap; echo "=== sdb.mk ==="; cat subprojects/sdb.mk | head -20

cd /workspace/radare2/subprojects && git clone --depth 1 --branch 2.4.6 https://github.com/radareorg/sdb.git sdb 2>&1 | tail -5; echo "=== sdb cloned ==="; ls sdb/src/sdb.h 2>/dev/null || find sdb -name "sdb.h" | head -5

cd /workspace/radare2 && clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I libr/include \
  -I subprojects/sdb/include \
  libr/util/queue.c -o /tmp/queue.bc 2>&1 | head -30
cd /workspace/radare2 && cat libr/util/debruijn.c; echo "=== debruijn header ==="; find . -name "r_debruijn.h" -exec cat {} \;
cd /workspace/radare2 && cat libr/include/r_util/r_stack.h; echo "=== r_base36 header ==="; cat libr/include/r_util/r_base36.h
find /workspace/klee -name "klee.h" | head -10; echo "=== include dir ==="; ls /workspace/klee/include/ 2>/dev/null; find /workspace/klee -path "*/klee/klee.h" | head -5

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses

# Compile harness_queue.c + queue.c to bitcode
clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I /workspace/radare2/libr/include \
  -I /workspace/radare2/subprojects/sdb/include \
  -I /workspace/klee/include \
  harness_queue.c -o harness_queue.bc 2>&1

echo "=== harness_queue.bc done ==="

clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I /workspace/radare2/libr/include \
  -I /workspace/radare2/subprojects/sdb/include \
  -I /workspace/klee/include \
  harness_stack.c -o harness_stack.bc 2>&1

echo "=== harness_stack.bc done ==="

clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I /workspace/radare2/libr/include \
  -I /workspace/radare2/subprojects/sdb/include \
  -I /workspace/klee/include \
  harness_base36.c -o harness_base36.bc 2>&1

echo "=== harness_base36.bc done ==="

clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I /workspace/radare2/libr/include \
  -I /workspace/radare2/subprojects/sdb/include \
  -I /workspace/klee/include \
  harness_debruijn.c -o harness_debruijn.bc 2>&1

echo "=== harness_debruijn.bc done ==="
ls -la *.bc

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses

# Recompile radare2 source files to bitcode
clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I /workspace/radare2/libr/include \
  -I /workspace/radare2/subprojects/sdb/include \
  /workspace/radare2/libr/util/queue.c -o queue.bc 2>&1

clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I /workspace/radare2/libr/include \
  -I /workspace/radare2/subprojects/sdb/include \
  /workspace/radare2/libr/util/stack.c -o stack.bc 2>&1

clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I /workspace/radare2/libr/include \
  -I /workspace/radare2/subprojects/sdb/include \
  /workspace/radare2/libr/util/base36.c -o base36.bc 2>&1

clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
  -I /workspace/radare2/libr/include \
  -I /workspace/radare2/subprojects/sdb/include \
  /workspace/radare2/libr/util/debruijn.c -o debruijn.bc 2>&1

echo "=== Source bitcode files compiled ==="
ls -la *.bc

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses

# Link harness with source bitcode using llvm-link
LLVM_LINK=$(which llvm-link)

$LLVM_LINK harness_queue.bc queue.bc -o linked_queue.bc 2>&1
echo "=== linked_queue ==="
$LLVM_LINK harness_stack.bc stack.bc -o linked_stack.bc 2>&1
echo "=== linked_stack ==="
$LLVM_LINK harness_base36.bc base36.bc -o linked_base36.bc 2>&1
echo "=== linked_base36 ==="
$LLVM_LINK harness_debruijn.bc debruijn.bc -o linked_debruijn.bc 2>&1
echo "=== linked_debruijn ==="

ls -la linked_*.bc

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses

# Now optimize the bitcode to simplify
opt -O2 -strip linked_queue.bc -o linked_queue_opt.bc 2>&1 | head -5
opt -O2 -strip linked_stack.bc -o linked_stack_opt.bc 2>&1 | head -5
opt -O2 -strip linked_base36.bc -o linked_base36_opt.bc 2>&1 | head -5
opt -O2 -strip linked_debruijn.bc -o linked_debruijn_opt.bc 2>&1 | head -5

echo "=== Optimized ==="
ls -la linked_*_opt.bc

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
opt -O2 linked_queue.bc -o linked_queue_opt.bc 2>&1 | head -5
opt -O2 linked_stack.bc -o linked_stack_opt.bc 2>&1 | head -5
opt -O2 linked_base36.bc -o linked_base36_opt.bc 2>&1 | head -5
opt -O2 linked_debruijn.bc -o linked_debruijn_opt.bc 2>&1 | head -5
echo "=== Optimized ==="
ls -la linked_*_opt.bc

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses

KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
mkdir -p /analysis-results/klee-queue

# Run KLEE on queue
timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-queue \
  --max-time=60 \
  --max-memory=2000 \
  --max-instructions=100000 \
  --use-batching-search \
  --batch-instructions=10000 \
  --max-symbolic-array-size=4096 \
  --disable-posix-runtime \
  linked_queue_opt.bc 2>&1 | tail -30

echo "=== KLEE queue done ==="
/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee --help 2>&1 | grep -E "max-time|max-memory|max-instructions|batching|batch|sym-array|posix|output-dir|libc|emit-all|only|search|max-forks|watchdog|use" | head -40
/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee --help 2>&1 | grep -E "max-time|max-memory|max-instr|max-fork|max-sym|output-dir|watchdog|emit-all|only-one|write|libc=none|external" | head -30

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses

KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-queue
mkdir -p /analysis-results/klee-queue

# Run KLEE on queue with correct options
timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-queue \
  --max-time=60 \
  --max-memory=2000 \
  --max-instructions=100000 \
  --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search \
  --batch-instructions=10000 \
  --search=dfs \
  --libc=none \
  linked_queue_opt.bc 2>&1 | tail -40

echo "=== KLEE queue done ==="

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-queue

timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-queue \
  --max-time=60 \
  --max-memory=2000 \
  --max-instructions=100000 \
  --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search \
  --batch-instructions=10000 \
  --search=dfs \
  --libc=none \
  linked_queue_opt.bc 2>&1 | tail -40

echo "=== KLEE queue done ==="

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-stack

timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-stack \
  --max-time=60 \
  --max-memory=2000 \
  --max-instructions=100000 \
  --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search \
  --batch-instructions=10000 \
  --search=dfs \
  --libc=none \
  linked_stack_opt.bc 2>&1 | tail -40

echo "=== KLEE stack done ==="

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-base36

timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-base36 \
  --max-time=60 \
  --max-memory=2000 \
  --max-instructions=100000 \
  --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search \
  --batch-instructions=10000 \
  --search=dfs \
  --libc=none \
  linked_base36_opt.bc 2>&1 | tail -40

echo "=== KLEE base36 done ==="

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-debruijn

timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-debruijn \
  --max-time=60 \
  --max-memory=2000 \
  --max-instructions=200000 \
  --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search \
  --batch-instructions=10000 \
  --search=dfs \
  --libc=none \
  linked_debruijn_opt.bc 2>&1 | tail -40

echo "=== KLEE debruijn done ==="

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
# Recompile debruijn without optimization - use the unoptimized linked version
KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-debruijn

timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-debruijn \
  --max-time=60 \
  --max-memory=2000 \
  --max-instructions=200000 \
  --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search \
  --batch-instructions=10000 \
  --search=dfs \
  --libc=none \
  linked_debruijn.bc 2>&1 | tail -40

echo "=== KLEE debruijn (unopt) done ==="

# Let's also compile a few more target files and create harnesses
# Let's look at more potential targets
cd /workspace/radare2
find libr/util -name "*.c" | xargs wc -l 2>/dev/null | sort -n | head -30

cd /workspace/radare2
# Let's look at base32 and base91 for more analysis targets
cat libr/include/r_util/r_base32.h; echo "=== base32.c ==="; cat libr/util/base32.c

cd /workspace/radare2
cat libr/include/r_util/r_bits.h 2>/dev/null; echo "=== bits.c ==="; cat libr/util/bits.c 2>/dev/null | head -80; echo "=== bitmap ==="; cat libr/include/r_util/r_bitmap.h 2>/dev/null

cd /workspace/radare2
# Compile more target files to bitcode
for f in libr/util/base32.c libr/util/bitmap.c libr/util/bloom.c; do
  echo "=== Compiling $f ==="
  clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone \
    -I libr/include -I subprojects/sdb/include \
    "$f" -o "/tmp/$(basename $f .c).bc" 2>&1 | head -5
done
echo "=== Done ==="; ls -la /tmp/base32.bc /tmp/bitmap.bc /tmp/bloom.bc 2>/dev/null

cd /workspace/radare2
# Check bloom filter API
cat libr/include/r_util/r_bloom.h 2>/dev/null || find . -name "r_bloom.h" -exec cat {} \; 2>/dev/null
echo "=== bloom.c ==="
cat libr/util/bloom.c

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
LLVM_LINK=$(which llvm-link)

# Link all new harnesses
$LLVM_LINK harness_base32.bc base32.bc -o linked_base32.bc 2>&1
$LLVM_LINK harness_bitmap.bc bitmap.bc -o linked_bitmap.bc 2>&1
$LLVM_LINK harness_bloom.bc bloom.bc -o linked_bloom.bc 2>&1

echo "=== Linked ==="
ls -la linked_base32.bc linked_bitmap.bc linked_bloom.bc

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee

# Run KLEE on base32
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-base32
timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-base32 \
  --max-time=60 --max-memory=2000 --max-instructions=100000 --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search --batch-instructions=10000 --search=dfs --libc=none \
  linked_base32.bc 2>&1 | tail -30
echo "=== KLEE base32 done ==="

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee

# Run KLEE on bitmap
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-bitmap
timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-bitmap \
  --max-time=60 --max-memory=2000 --max-instructions=100000 --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search --batch-instructions=10000 --search=dfs --libc=none \
  linked_bitmap.bc 2>&1 | tail -30
echo "=== KLEE bitmap done ==="

cd /workspace/klee_harnesses
KLEE_BIN=/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee

# Run KLEE on bloom
rm -rf /analysis-results/klee-bloom
timeout 120 $KLEE_BIN \
  --output-dir=/analysis-results/klee-bloom \
  --max-time=60 --max-memory=2000 --max-instructions=100000 --max-forks=1000 \
  --use-batching-search --batch-instructions=10000 --search=dfs --libc=none \
  linked_bloom.bc 2>&1 | tail -30

# KLEE Symbolic Execution Analysis Report: radare2

## Overview

This report documents the results of running **KLEE** (Symbolic Virtual Machine built on LLVM) 
on selected components of the **radare2** project (https://github.com/radareorg/radare2).

## Tool Information

- **KLEE Version**: 3.3-pre (build revision 1fc4873a4be52116dda319d7de3cb8d01ea25c1b)

- **KLEE Source**: https://github.com/klee/klee

## Analysis Methodology

1. **Target Selection**: Selected utility functions from radare2's `libr/util/` directory 
   that have clear input/output interfaces suitable for symbolic execution.
   
2. **Harness Creation**: Created C harness files that make inputs symbolic using

## Findings

### 1. Queue (libr/util/queue.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Concretized symbolic size** (queue.c:13): When `r_queue_new` is called with a 
  symbolic capacity, KLEE must concretize the allocation size. This is expected behavior 
  when symbolic values are used for memory allocation sizes.
- **ASSERTION FAIL** (harness_queue.c:31): KLEE found a path where the assertion 
  `klee_assert(0)` is triggered, indicating that the dequeue operation returns NULL 
  when the queue is not empty (symbolic execution found a path where the dequeue 
  returns NULL despite elements being enqueued). This may indicate a potential issue 
  with the queue's capacity management when symbolic values are involved.

### 2. Stack (libr/util/stack.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Concretized symbolic size** (stack.c:11): Same as queue - symbolic allocation size.
- **Failed external call: r_assert_log** (stack.c:44): The `r_stack_push` function 
  calls `r_assert_log` which is an external function not modeled in KLEE's environment. 
  This indicates the stack push operation triggers an assertion check that references 
  an external logging function.

### 3. Base36 (libr/util/base36.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Out of bound pointer** (base36.c:68): KLEE found memory safety issues in 
  `b36_tonum()`. The function accesses `index36[(unsigned char)*s]` where `*s` comes 
  from a symbolic input string. The index36 array has 0xff (255) entries, but if the 
  input contains bytes >= 0xff, the array access could be out of bounds. The 
  symbolic execution found specific inputs that trigger this memory safety violation.

  **Details**: The address expression shows `(ZExt w64 (Read w8 0 sym_str))` being 
  used as an index into the pow36 array, which when multiplied by 4 and added to the 
  base address, results in an out-of-bounds memory access. This is a potential buffer 
  over-read vulnerability.

### 4. De Bruijn (libr/util/debruijn.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **Concretized symbolic size** (debruijn.c:51): The `calloc` call with symbolic 
  `maxlen` parameter causes concretization. The function ran until the instruction 
  limit was reached (200,000 instructions), indicating complex recursive control flow 
  in the de Bruijn sequence generation.

### 5. Base32 (libr/util/base32.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **External call with symbolic argument: toupper** (base32.c:115): The 
  `base32_decode_ut64` function calls `toupper()` with a symbolic character argument. 
  KLEE cannot model this external call with symbolic arguments, which prevents full 
  symbolic execution of the decode path.

### 6. Bitmap (libr/util/bitmap.c)

**Errors Found**: 0
- No errors found. The bitmap operations (set, unset, test, count) executed 
  successfully with symbolic bit positions. The assertions in the harness were 
  satisfied, indicating the bitmap implementation is correct for the tested 
  properties.

### 7. Bloom Filter (libr/util/bloom.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Concretized symbolic size** (bloom.c:43, bloom.c:47): Both `malloc` and `calloc` 
  calls with symbolic `m` and `k` parameters cause concretization. The bloom filter 
  implementation itself appears correct - the assertion that `r_bloom_check` returns 
  true after `r_bloom_add` was satisfied.

### 8. Getopt (libr/util/getopt.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **External call with symbolic argument: strchr** (getopt.c:48): The `r_getopt_next` 
  function calls `strchr` with a symbolic option character. Despite this, KLEE 
  successfully explored 501 paths and generated 339 test cases, demonstrating 
  extensive coverage of the option parsing logic including various option combinations.

### 9. Random Art (libr/util/randomart.c)

**Errors Found**: 0
- No errors found. The `r_print_randomart` function executed successfully with 
  symbolic digest data and address. The assertion that the output starts with '+' 
  (the border character) was satisfied.

## Key Findings

### Potential Memory Safety Issue in b36_tonum() (base36.c:68)

The most significant finding is a potential out-of-bounds read in the `b36_tonum()` 
function. The `index36` array is declared with 0xff (255) entries:
```c
static const int index36[0xff] = { ... };
```
When `*s` has the value 0xff (255), the access `index36[(unsigned char)*s]` accesses 
`index36[255]`, which is the 256th element of a 255-element array (indices 0-254). 
This is a classic off-by-one buffer over-read vulnerability.

The `pow36` array access `pow36[pos] * idx` is also concerning since `pos` can grow 
without bound based on input length, potentially exceeding the 14-element array.

## Test Case Generation

KLEE generated a total of **388 test cases** across all targets. These test cases 
represent concrete inputs that explore different execution paths, including:
- Paths that trigger errors (out-of-bound access, assertion failures)
- Paths that exercise normal functionality
- Edge cases for boundary conditions

### KLEE Build
- Location: /workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
- Built with Z3 solver support
- LLVM 18.1.3

### Harnesses
- Location: /workspace/klee_harnesses/

- Location: /analysis-results/

  klee-base32, klee-bitmap, klee-bloom, klee-getopt, klee-randomart)
- Each contains: .ktest files, .err files, .kquery files, messages.txt, run.istats

## Conclusion

KLEE symbolic execution successfully identified:
1. A potential out-of-bounds read vulnerability in `b36_tonum()` (base36.c)
2. Symbolic size concretization issues in memory allocation paths
3. External call limitations with symbolic arguments in several functions
4. Assertion failure in queue dequeue behavior with symbolic capacity

The analysis generated 388 test cases covering diverse execution paths across 
9 radare2 utility components, providing valuable coverage and identifying 
potential issues for further investigation.

KLEE Symbolic Virtual Machine
=============================

[![Build Status](https://github.com/klee/klee/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/klee/klee/actions?query=workflow%3ACI)
[![Coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/klee/klee/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/klee/klee)

`KLEE` is a symbolic virtual machine built on top of the LLVM compiler
infrastructure. Currently, there are two primary components:

  1. The core symbolic virtual machine engine; this is responsible for
     executing LLVM bitcode modules with support for symbolic
     values. This is comprised of the code in lib/.

  2. A POSIX/Linux emulation layer oriented towards supporting uClibc,
     with additional support for making parts of the operating system
     environment symbolic.

Additionally, there is a simple library for replaying computed inputs
on native code (for closed programs). There is also a more complicated
infrastructure for replaying the inputs generated for the POSIX/Linux
emulation layer, which handles running native programs in an
environment that matches a computed test input, including setting up
files, pipes, environment variables, and passing command line
arguments.

For further information, see the [webpage](https://klee-se.org/).
=== CMake requirements ===
# Find LLVM
find_package(LLVM REQUIRED CONFIG HINTS "${LLVM_DIR}")
message(STATUS "LLVM directory ${LLVM_DIR}")
if (LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR LESS 15)
  message(FATAL_ERROR "KLEE requires LLVM 15 or newer")
set(LLVMCC "${LLVM_TOOLS_BINARY_DIR}/clang"
set(LLVMCXX "${LLVM_TOOLS_BINARY_DIR}/clang++"
if (LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS)
  # Certain LLVM debugging macros only work when LLVM was built with asserts
# This is likely a bad idea because some of LLVM's header files use the NDEBUG
if (LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS AND (NOT ENABLE_KLEE_ASSERTS))
    "LLVM was built with assertions but KLEE will be built without them.\n"
elseif ((NOT LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS) AND ENABLE_KLEE_ASSERTS)

# Set the default so that if the following is true:
# * Z3 was found

#

if (Z3_FOUND)

  if (Z3_FOUND)

    set(ENABLE_Z3 1) # For config.h

      string(REPLACE ".so" ".dylib" Z3_LIBRARIES ${Z3_LIBRARIES})
      message(STATUS "New Z3 library path: ${Z3_LIBRARIES}")

      if(EXISTS "${Z3_LIBRARIES}")
        message(STATUS "Found Z3 library on MacOS")

#include <r_util.h>

R_API RQueue *r_queue_new(int n) {
	if (n <= 0) {
		return NULL;
	}
	RQueue *q = R_NEW0 (RQueue);
	if (!q) {
		return NULL;
	}
	q->elems = R_NEWS0 (void *, n);
	if (!q->elems) {
		free (q);
		return NULL;
	}
	q->front = 0;
	q->rear = -1;
	q->size = 0;
	q->capacity = n;
	return q;
}

R_API void r_queue_free(RQueue *q) {
	if (q) {
		free (q->elems);
		free (q);
	}
}

static int is_full(RQueue *q) {
	 return q->size == q->capacity;
}

static int increase_capacity(RQueue *q) {
	unsigned int new_capacity = q->capacity * 2;
	void **newelems;
	int i, tmp_front;

	newelems = R_NEWS0(void *, new_capacity);
	if (!newelems) {
		return false;
	}

	i = -1;
	tmp_front = q->front;
	while (i + 1 < q->size) {
		i++;
		newelems[i] = q->elems[tmp_front];
		tmp_front = (tmp_front + 1) % q->capacity;

	free (q->elems);
	q->elems = newelems;
	q->front = 0;
	q->rear = i;
	q->capacity = new_capacity;
	return true;
}

R_API int r_queue_enqueue(RQueue *q, void *el) {
	if (is_full (q)) {
		int res = increase_capacity (q);
		if (!res) {
			return false;
		}
	}

	q->rear = (q->rear + 1) % q->capacity;
	q->elems[q->rear] = el;
	q->size++;
	return true;
}

R_API void *r_queue_dequeue(RQueue *q) {
	void *res;

	if (r_queue_is_empty (q)) {
		return NULL;
	}
	res = q->elems[q->front];
	q->front = (q->front + 1) % q->capacity;
	q->size--;
	return res;
}

R_API int r_queue_is_empty(RQueue *q) {
	return q->size == 0;
}

#include <r_util.h>

// The following two (commented out) lines are the character set used in peda.
// You may use this charset instead of the A-Za-z0-9 charset normally used.
// char* peda_charset =
//    "A%sB$nC-(D;)Ea0Fb1Gc2Hd3Ie4Jf5Kg6Lh7Mi8Nj9OkPlQmRnSoTpUqVrWsXtYuZvwxyz";

//TODO(crowell): Make charset configurable, allow banning characters.
static const char debruijn_charset[] = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz1234567890";

// Generate a De Bruijn sequence.
// pnl = prenecklace
// lnp = lyndon prefix
static void de_bruijn_seq(int pnl_len_t, int lnp_len_p, int order,
		int maxlen, int size, int* pnl_a, char* sequence, const char* charset) {
	R_RETURN_IF_FAIL (charset && sequence);
	if (strlen (sequence) == maxlen) {
		return;
	}
	int i;
	if (pnl_len_t > order) {
		if (order % lnp_len_p == 0) {
			for (i = 1; i <= lnp_len_p; i++) {
				sequence[strlen (sequence)] = charset[pnl_a[i]];
				if (strlen (sequence) == maxlen) {
					return;
				}
			}
		}
	} else {
		pnl_a[pnl_len_t] = pnl_a[pnl_len_t - lnp_len_p];
		de_bruijn_seq (pnl_len_t + 1, lnp_len_p, order, maxlen, size, pnl_a, sequence, charset);
		for (i = pnl_a[pnl_len_t - lnp_len_p] + 1; i < size; i++) {
			pnl_a[pnl_len_t] = i;
			de_bruijn_seq (pnl_len_t + 1, pnl_len_t, order, maxlen,
					size, pnl_a, sequence, charset);
		}
	}
}

// Generate a De Bruijn sequence.
// Returns a string in the heap, caller must free the memory.
static char* de_bruijn(const char* charset, int order, int maxlen) {
	R_RETURN_VAL_IF_FAIL (charset, NULL);
	size_t size = strlen (charset);
	char *sequence = NULL;
	int* pnl_a = calloc (size * (size_t)order, sizeof (int));
	if (pnl_a) {
		sequence = calloc (maxlen + 1, 1);
		if (sequence) {
			de_bruijn_seq (1, 1, order, maxlen, size, pnl_a, sequence, charset);
		}
		free (pnl_a);
	}
	return sequence;
}

// Generate a cyclic pattern of desired size, and charset, return with starting
// offset of start.
// The returned string is malloced, and it is the responsibility of the caller
// to free the memory.
R_API char* r_debruijn_pattern(int size, int start, const char* charset) {
	size_t len;
	if (!charset) {
		charset = debruijn_charset;
	}
	if (start >= size) {
		return (char*)NULL;
	}
	char *pat = de_bruijn (charset, 3 /*subsequence length*/, size);
	if (!pat) {
		return NULL;
	}
	if (start == 0) {
		len = strlen (pat);
		if (size != len) {
			R_LOG_WARN ("requested pattern of length %d, generated length %d", size, (int)len);
		}
		return pat;
	}
	char *pat2 = malloc ((size - start) + 1);
	if (pat2) {
		r_str_ncpy (pat2, pat + start, size - start);
		len = strlen (pat2);
		if (size != len) {
			R_LOG_WARN ("requested pattern of length %d, generated length %d", size, (int)len);
		}
	}
	free (pat);
	return pat2;
}

// Finds the offset of a given value in a cyclic pattern of an integer.
R_API int r_debruijn_offset(ut64 value, bool is_big_endian) {
	// 0x10000 should be long enough. This is how peda works, and nobody complains
	// ... but is slow. Optimize for common case.
	int i, lens[2] = {0x1000, 0x10000};
	int retval = -1;
	char buf[9];
	if (value != 0 && value != UT64_MAX && value != UT32_MAX) {
		for (i = 0; i < 2 && retval == -1; i++) {
			char *pattern = r_debruijn_pattern (lens[i], 0, debruijn_charset);
			buf[8] = '\0';
			r_write_ble64 (buf, value, is_big_endian);
			char *needle = buf;
			for (; !*needle; needle++) {
				/* do nothing here */
			}
			char* pch = strstr (pattern, needle);
			if (pch) {
				retval = (int)(size_t)(pch - pattern);
			}
			free (pattern);
		}
	}
	return retval;
}

/* radare - LGPL - Copyright 2024 - pancake */

#include <r_util.h>
#include <r_util/r_base32.h>

static const char base32_alphabet[] = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567";
static const char base32_padding = '=';

// Utility function to find index in base32 alphabet
static int base32_char_index(char c) {
	if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') {
		return c - 'A';
	}
	if (c >= '2' && c <= '7') {
		return c - '2' + 26;
	}
	return -1;
}

R_API char *r_base32_encode(const ut8 *data, size_t input_length, size_t *output_length) {
	const size_t encoded_size = (input_length + 4) / 5 * 8;
	char *encoded_data = (char *)malloc (encoded_size + 1);
	if (!encoded_data) {
		return NULL;
	}

	size_t i, j, index;
	int current_byte, next_byte;
	for (i = 0, j = 0; i < input_length;) {
		current_byte = data[i++] << 8;
		if (i < input_length) current_byte |= data[i++];
		current_byte <<= 8;
		if (i < input_length) current_byte |= data[i++];
		current_byte <<= 8;
		if (i < input_length) current_byte |= data[i++];
		current_byte <<= 8;
		if (i < input_length) current_byte |= data[i++];

		for (index = 0; index < 8; index++) {
			next_byte = (current_byte & 0xF8000000) >> 27;
			encoded_data[j++] = base32_alphabet[next_byte];
			current_byte <<= 5;
		}
	}

	while (j < encoded_size) {
		encoded_data[j++] = base32_padding;
	}
	encoded_data[encoded_size] = '\0';

	if (output_length) {
		*output_length = encoded_size;
	}
	return encoded_data;
}

R_API ut8 *r_base32_decode(const char *data, size_t input_length, size_t *output_length) {
	if (input_length % 8 != 0) {
		return NULL;
	}

	size_t decoded_size = input_length * 5 / 8;
	unsigned char *decoded_data = (unsigned char *)malloc (decoded_size);
	if (!decoded_data) {
		return NULL;
	}

	size_t i, j, index;
	int current_byte, next_byte;
	for (i = 0, j = 0; i < input_length;) {
		current_byte = 0;
		for (index = 0; index < 8 && i < input_length; index++) {
			next_byte = base32_char_index (toupper (data[i++]));
			if (next_byte == -1) {
				free (decoded_data);
				return NULL;
			}
			current_byte = (current_byte << 5) | next_byte;
		}

		for (index = 0; index < 5; index++) {
			decoded_data[j++] = (current_byte & 0xFF000000) >> 24;
			current_byte <<= 8;
		}
	}

	if (output_length) {
		*output_length = decoded_size;
	}
	return decoded_data;
}

R_API char *base32_encode_ut64(ut64 input) {
	size_t encoded_size = 13; // Maximum 13 characters for 64-bit input
	char *encoded_data = (char *)malloc (encoded_size + 1);
	if (!encoded_data) {
		return NULL;
	}

	int i;
	for (i = 12; i >= 0; i--) {
		encoded_data[i] = base32_alphabet[input & 0x1F];
		input >>= 5;
	}
	encoded_data[encoded_size] = '\0';

	return encoded_data;
}

// Decode function for ut64
R_API ut64 base32_decode_ut64(const char *input) {
	ut64 decoded_value = 0;
	int i;
	for (i = 0; i < 13; i++) {
		int index = base32_char_index (toupper (input[i]));
		if (index == -1) {
			return 0;
		}
		decoded_value = (decoded_value << 5) | index;
	}
	return decoded_value;
}

static inline int r_bits_popcount32(ut32 x) {

static inline int r_bits_popcount64(ut64 x) {

	if (!(x & 0xF000000000000000ULL)) { n += 4;  x <<= 4; }
	if (!(x & 0xC000000000000000ULL)) { n += 2;  x <<= 2; }
	if (!(x & 0x8000000000000000ULL)) { n += 1; }
	return n;

/* radare - MIT - Copyright 2025 - pancake */

#include <r_util/r_bloom.h>

typedef struct r_bloom_t {
	size_t m; // number of bits
	size_t k; // number of hash functions
	ut8 *bit_array; // bit vector
	size_t array_size; // in bytes (m + 7) / 8
	RBloomHashFunc *hash_funcs;
} RBloom;

#define BF_BIT_SET(arr, i)   ((arr)[(i)/8] |= (1 << ((i) % 8)))
#define BF_BIT_CHECK(arr, i) ((arr)[(i)/8] & (1 << ((i) % 8)))

// A simple djb2-variant hash function that supports binary data
static ut32 default_bloom_hash(const void *data, size_t len, ut32 seed) {
	const ut8 *ptr = (const ut8*) data;
	ut32 hash = 5381 ^ seed;
	size_t i;
	for (i = 0; i < len; i++) {
		hash = ((hash << 5) + hash) + ptr[i]; /* hash * 33 + c */
	}
	return hash;
}

R_API RBloom * R_NULLABLE r_bloom_new(size_t m, size_t k, RBloomHashFunc * hash_funcs) {
	if (m == 0 || k == 0) {
		return NULL;
	}
	RBloom *bf = R_NEW (RBloom);
	if (!r_bloom_init (bf, m, k, hash_funcs)) {
		R_FREE (bf);
	}
	return bf;
}

R_API bool r_bloom_init(RBloom *bf, size_t m, size_t k, RBloomHashFunc * hash_funcs) {
	R_RETURN_VAL_IF_FAIL (bf, false);
	bf->m = m;
	bf->k = k;
	bf->array_size = (m + 7) / 8;
	bf->bit_array = (ut8*) calloc (bf->array_size, sizeof (ut8));
	if (! bf->bit_array) {
		return false;
	}
	bf->hash_funcs = (RBloomHashFunc *) malloc (k * sizeof (RBloomHashFunc));
	if (! bf->hash_funcs) {
		free (bf->bit_array);
		return false;
	}
	if (hash_funcs) {
		memcpy (bf->hash_funcs, hash_funcs, k * sizeof (RBloomHashFunc));
	} else {
		size_t i;
		for (i = 0; i < k; i++) {
			bf->hash_funcs[i] = default_bloom_hash;
		}
	}
	return true;
}

R_API void r_bloom_reset(RBloom *bf) {
	R_RETURN_IF_FAIL (bf);
	size_t m = bf->m;
	size_t k = bf->k;
	RBloomHashFunc *funcs = bf->hash_funcs;
	bf->hash_funcs = NULL;
	r_bloom_fini (bf);
	r_bloom_init (bf, m, k, funcs);
	free (funcs);
}

R_API void r_bloom_fini(RBloom * R_NULLABLE bf) {
	R_RETURN_IF_FAIL (bf);
	free (bf->bit_array);
	free (bf->hash_funcs);
}

R_API void r_bloom_free(RBloom * R_NULLABLE bf) {
	if (bf) {
		r_bloom_fini (bf);
		free (bf);
	}
}

static ut32 seedfrom(ut32 index) {
	// Mix the bits of 'index' to produce a more entropic seed.
	index = (index ^ 61) ^ (index >> 16);
	index = index + (index << 3);
	index = index ^ (index >> 4);
	index = index * 0x27d4eb2d;
	index = index ^ (index >> 15);
	return index;
}

R_API bool r_bloom_add(RBloom *bf, const void * data, size_t len) {
	R_RETURN_VAL_IF_FAIL (bf && data, false);
	bool changed = false;
	size_t i;
	for (i = 0; i < bf->k; i++) {
		ut32 hash = bf->hash_funcs[i] (data, len, seedfrom (i));
		size_t index = hash % bf->m;
#if 0
		BF_BIT_SET (bf->bit_array, index);
#else
		if (!BF_BIT_CHECK (bf->bit_array, index)) {
			changed = true;
		}
		BF_BIT_SET(bf->bit_array, index);
#endif
	}
	return changed;
}

R_API bool r_bloom_check(RBloom *bf, const void * data, size_t len) {
	R_RETURN_VAL_IF_FAIL (bf && data, false);
	size_t i;
	for (i = 0; i < bf->k; i++) {
		ut32 hash = bf->hash_funcs[i] (data, len, seedfrom (i));
		size_t index = hash % bf->m;
		if (! BF_BIT_CHECK (bf->bit_array, index)) {
			return false;
		}
	}
	return true;
}

/*
 * This code is originally taken from OpenSSH:
 * https://cvsweb.openbsd.org/cgi-bin/cvsweb/src/usr.bin/ssh/key.c?rev=1.75&content-type=text/x-cvsweb-markup
 */

/*
 * Draw an ASCII-Art representing the fingerprint so human brain can
 * profit from its built-in pattern recognition ability.
 * This technique is called "random art" and can be found in some
 * scientific publications like this original paper:
 *
 * "Hash Visualization: a New Technique to improve Real-World Security",
 * Perrig A. and Song D., 1999, International Workshop on Cryptographic
 * Techniques and E-Commerce (CrypTEC '99)
 * sparrow.ece.cmu.edu/~adrian/projects/validation/validation.pdf
 *
 * The subject came up in a talk by Dan Kaminsky, too.
 *
 * If you see the picture is different, the key is different.
 * If the picture looks the same, you still know nothing.
 *
 * The algorithm used here is a worm crawling over a discrete plane,
 * leaving a trace (augmenting the field) everywhere it goes.
 * Movement is taken from dgst_raw 2bit-wise.  Bumping into walls
 * makes the respective movement vector be ignored for this turn.
 * Graphs are not unambiguous, because circles in graphs can be
 * walked in either direction.
 */

/*
 * Field sizes for the random art.  Have to be odd, so the starting point
 * can be in the exact middle of the picture, and FLDBASE should be >=8 .
 * Else pictures would be too dense, and drawing the frame would
 * fail, too, because the key type would not fit in anymore.
 */
#include <r_util.h>

#define	FLDBASE		8
#define	FLDSIZE_Y	(FLDBASE + 1)
#define	FLDSIZE_X	(FLDBASE * 2 + 1)

//static char * key_fingerprint_randomart(ut8 *dgst_raw, ut32 dgst_raw_len) {
R_API char *r_print_randomart(const ut8 *dgst_raw, ut32 dgst_raw_len, ut64 addr) {
	/*
	 * Chars to be used after each other every time the worm
	 * intersects with itself.  Matter of taste.
	 */
	char *augmentation_string = " .o+=*BOX@%&#/^SE";
	char *p;
	ut8 field[FLDSIZE_X][FLDSIZE_Y];
	ut32 i, b;
	size_t len = strlen (augmentation_string) - 1;
	// 2*(FLDSIZE_X+3) there are two for loops that iterate over this
	// FLDSIZE_Y * (FLDSIZE_X+3) there is a loop that for each y iterates over the whole FLDSIZE_X
	// The rest is counting the +--[0x%08"PFMT64x"]- and '\0'
	size_t retval_sz = 2 * (FLDSIZE_X + 3) + (FLDSIZE_Y * (FLDSIZE_X+3))+ 7 + sizeof (PFMT64x);
	char *retval = calloc (1, retval_sz);

	/* initialize field */
	memset (field, 0, FLDSIZE_X * FLDSIZE_Y * sizeof (char));
	int x = FLDSIZE_X / 2;
	int y = FLDSIZE_Y / 2;

	/* process raw key */
	for (i = 0; i < dgst_raw_len; i++) {
		/* each byte conveys four 2-bit move commands */
		int input = dgst_raw[i];
		for (b = 0; b < 4; b++) {
			/* evaluate 2 bit, rest is shifted later */
			x += (input & 0x1) ? 1 : -1;
			y += (input & 0x2) ? 1 : -1;

			/* assure we are still in bounds */
			x = R_MAX (x, 0);
			y = R_MAX (y, 0);
			x = R_MIN (x, FLDSIZE_X - 1);
			y = R_MIN (y, FLDSIZE_Y - 1);

			/* augment the field */
			if (field[x][y] < len - 2) {
				field[x][y]++;
			}
			input = input >> 2;
		}
	}

	/* mark starting point and end point*/
	field[FLDSIZE_X / 2][FLDSIZE_Y / 2] = len - 1;
	field[x][y] = len;

	/* fill in retval */
	snprintf (retval, retval_sz, "+--[0x%08"PFMT64x"]-", addr);
	p = strchr (retval, '\0');

	/* output upper border */
	for (i = p - retval - 1; i < FLDSIZE_X; i++) {
		*p++ = '-';
	}
	*p++ = '+';
	*p++ = '\n';

  echo ""
done

{"command": "# Now let's create a comprehensive summary report
cat > /analysis-results/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md << 'REPORT'
# KLEE Symbolic Execution Analysis Report: radare2

## Overview

This report documents the results of running **KLEE** (Symbolic Virtual Machine built on LLVM) 
on selected components of the **radare2** project (https://github.com/radareorg/radare2).

## Tool Information

- **KLEE Version**: 3.3-pre (build revision 1fc4873a4be52116dda319d7de3cb8d01ea25c1b)
- **LLVM Version**: 18.1.3
- **Solver Backend**: Z3 (version 4.8.12)
- **Build Mode**: Release (Asserts: ON)
- **KLEE Source**: https://github.com/klee/klee

## Analysis Methodology

1. **Target Selection**: Selected utility functions from radare2's `libr/util/` directory 
   that have clear input/output interfaces suitable for symbolic execution.
   
2. **Harness Creation**: Created C harness files that make inputs symbolic using 
   `klee_make_symbolic()` and verify properties using `klee_assert()`.

3. **Compilation**: Compiled both harnesses and target source files to LLVM bitcode 
   using `clang -emit-llvm -c -g -O0 -Xclang -disable-O0-optnone`.

4. **Linking**: Linked harness bitcode with source bitcode using `llvm-link`.

5. **Execution**: Ran KLEE with DFS search strategy, Z3 solver backend, and 
   `--libc=none` (freestanding environment).

## Target Files Analyzed

| # | Source File | Lines | Functions Analyzed |
|---|------------|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | libr/util/queue.c | 90 | r_queue_new, r_queue_enqueue, r_queue_dequeue, r_queue_free |
| 2 | libr/util/stack.c | 89 | r_stack_new, r_stack_push, r_stack_pop, r_stack_free |
| 3 | libr/util/base36.c | 77 | b36_fromnum, b36_tonum |
| 4 | libr/util/debruijn.c | 119 | r_debruijn_pattern, r_debruijn_offset |
| 5 | libr/util/base32.c | 122 | r_base32_encode, r_base32_decode, base32_encode_ut64, base32_decode_ut64 |
| 6 | libr/util/bitmap.c | ~150 | r_bitmap_new, r_bitmap_set, r_bitmap_unset, r_bitmap_test, r_bitmap_count |
| 7 | libr/util/bloom.c | 128 | r_bloom_new, r_bloom_add, r_bloom_check, r_bloom_free |
| 8 | libr/util/getopt.c | 91 | r_getopt_init, r_getopt_next |
| 9 | libr/util/randomart.c | 121 | r_print_randomart |

## Results Summary

| Target | Completed Paths | Partial Paths | Total Tests | Errors Found | Total Instructions | Total Queries |
|--------|-----------------|---------------|-------------|--------------|-------------------|--------------|
| queue | 1 | 5 | 3 | 2 | 448 | 21 |
| stack | 1 | 5 | 3 | 2 | 347 | 14 |
| base36 | 32 | 30 | 34 | 2 | 1,526 | 1,069 |
| debruijn | 1 | 2 | 3 | 1 | 200,000 | 13 |
| base32 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 324 | 15 |
| bitmap | 2 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 568 | 18 |
| bloom | - | - | 2 | 2 | - | - |
| getopt | 338 | 163 | 339 | 1 | 31,606 | 119 |
| randomart | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 2,928 | 29 |
| **TOTAL** | **375** | **207** | **388** | **11** | **237,143** | **1,298** |

## Findings

### 1. Queue (libr/util/queue.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Concretized symbolic size** (queue.c:13): When `r_queue_new` is called with a 
  symbolic capacity, KLEE must concretize the allocation size. This is expected behavior 
  when symbolic values are used for memory allocation sizes.
- **ASSERTION FAIL** (harness_queue.c:31): KLEE found a path where the assertion 
  `klee_assert(0)` is triggered, indicating that the dequeue operation returns NULL 
  when the queue is not empty (symbolic execution found a path where the dequeue 
  returns NULL despite elements being enqueued). This may indicate a potential issue 
  with the queue's capacity management when symbolic values are involved.

### 2. Stack (libr/util/stack.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Concretized symbolic size** (stack.c:11): Same as queue - symbolic allocation size.
- **Failed external call: r_assert_log** (stack.c:44): The `r_stack_push` function 
  calls `r_assert_log` which is an external function not modeled in KLEE's environment. 
  This indicates the stack push operation triggers an assertion check that references 
  an external logging function.

### 3. Base36 (libr/util/base36.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Out of bound pointer** (base36.c:68): KLEE found memory safety issues in 
  `b36_tonum()`. The function accesses `index36[(unsigned char)*s]` where `*s` comes 
  from a symbolic input string. The index36 array has 0xff (255) entries, but if the 
  input contains bytes >= 0xff, the array access could be out of bounds. The 
  symbolic execution found specific inputs that trigger this memory safety violation.

  **Details**: The address expression shows `(ZExt w64 (Read w8 0 sym_str))` being 
  used as an index into the pow36 array, which when multiplied by 4 and added to the 
  base address, results in an out-of-bounds memory access. This is a potential buffer 
  over-read vulnerability.

### 4. De Bruijn (libr/util/debruijn.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **Concretized symbolic size** (debruijn.c:51): The `calloc` call with symbolic 
  `maxlen` parameter causes concretization. The function ran until the instruction 
  limit was reached (200,000 instructions), indicating complex recursive control flow 
  in the de Bruijn sequence generation.

### 5. Base32 (libr/util/base32.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **External call with symbolic argument: toupper** (base32.c:115): The 
  `base32_decode_ut64` function calls `toupper()` with a symbolic character argument. 
  KLEE cannot model this external call with symbolic arguments, which prevents full 
  symbolic execution of the decode path.

### 6. Bitmap (libr/util/bitmap.c)

**Errors Found**: 0
- No errors found. The bitmap operations (set, unset, test, count) executed 
  successfully with symbolic bit positions. The assertions in the harness were 
  satisfied, indicating the bitmap implementation is correct for the tested 
  properties.

### 7. Bloom Filter (libr/util/bloom.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Concretized symbolic size** (bloom.c:43, bloom.c:47): Both `malloc` and `calloc` 
  calls with symbolic `m` and `k` parameters cause concretization. The bloom filter 
  implementation itself appears correct - the assertion that `r_bloom_check` returns 
  true after `r_bloom_add` was satisfied.

### 8. Getopt (libr/util/getopt.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **External call with symbolic argument: strchr** (getopt.c:48): The `r_getopt_next` 
  function calls `strchr` with a symbolic option character. Despite this, KLEE 
  successfully explored 501 paths and generated 339 test cases, demonstrating 
  extensive coverage of the option parsing logic including various option combinations.

### 9. Random Art (libr/util/randomart.c)

**Errors Found**: 0
- No errors found. The `r_print_randomart` function executed successfully with 
  symbolic digest data and address. The assertion that the output starts with '+' 
  (the border character) was satisfied.

## Key Findings

### Potential Memory Safety Issue in b36_tonum() (base36.c:68)

The most significant finding is a potential out-of-bounds read in the `b36_tonum()` 
function. The `index36` array is declared with 0xff (255) entries:
```c
static const int index36[0xff] = { ... };
```
When `*s` has the value 0xff (255), the access `index36[(unsigned char)*s]` accesses 
`index36[255]`, which is the 256th element of a 255-element array (indices 0-254). 
This is a classic off-by-one buffer over-read vulnerability.

The `pow36` array access `pow36[pos] * idx` is also concerning since `pos` can grow 
without bound based on input length, potentially exceeding the 14-element array.

## Test Case Generation

KLEE generated a total of **388 test cases** across all targets. These test cases 
represent concrete inputs that explore different execution paths, including:
- Paths that trigger errors (out-of-bound access, assertion failures)
- Paths that exercise normal functionality
- Edge cases for boundary conditions

## Tools and Artifacts

### KLEE Build
- Location: /workspace/klee/build/bin/klee
- Built with Z3 solver support
- LLVM 18.1.3

### Harnesses
- Location: /workspace/klee_harnesses/
- 9 harness files created for different radare2 components

### Analysis Results
- Location: /analysis-results/
- 9 result directories (klee-queue, klee-stack, klee-base36, klee-debruijn, 
  klee-base32, klee-bitmap, klee-bloom, klee-getopt, klee-randomart)
- Each contains: .ktest files, .err files, .kquery files, messages.txt, run.istats

## Conclusion

KLEE symbolic execution successfully identified:
1. A potential out-of-bounds read vulnerability in `b36_tonum()` (base36.c)
2. Symbolic size concretization issues in memory allocation paths
3. External call limitations with symbolic arguments in several functions
4. Assertion failure in queue dequeue behavior with symbolic capacity

The analysis generated 388 test cases covering diverse execution paths across 
9 radare2 utility components, providing valuable coverage and identifying 
potential issues for further investigation.
REPORT

echo "Report created"
wc -l /analysis-results/ANALYSIS_REPORT.md"}

   `--libc=none` (freestanding environment).

### 1. Queue (libr/util/queue.c)

**Errors Found**: 2

  symbolic capacity, KLEE must concretize the allocation size. This is expected behavior 
  when symbolic values are used for memory allocation sizes.

  `klee_assert(0)` is triggered, indicating that the dequeue operation returns NULL 
  when the queue is not empty (symbolic execution found a path where the dequeue 
  returns NULL despite elements being enqueued). This may indicate a potential issue 
  with the queue's capacity management when symbolic values are involved.

### 2. Stack (libr/util/stack.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Concretized symbolic size** (stack.c:11): Same as queue - symbolic allocation size.
- **Failed external call: r_assert_log** (stack.c:44): The `r_stack_push` function 
  calls `r_assert_log` which is an external function not modeled in KLEE's environment. 
  This indicates the stack push operation triggers an assertion check that references 
  an external logging function.

### 3. Base36 (libr/util/base36.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Out of bound pointer** (base36.c:68): KLEE found memory safety issues in 
  `b36_tonum()`. The function accesses `index36[(unsigned char)*s]` where `*s` comes 
  from a symbolic input string. The index36 array has 0xff (255) entries, but if the 
  input contains bytes >= 0xff, the array access could be out of bounds. The 
  symbolic execution found specific inputs that trigger this memory safety violation.

  **Details**: The address expression shows `(ZExt w64 (Read w8 0 sym_str))` being 
  used as an index into the pow36 array, which when multiplied by 4 and added to the 
  base address, results in an out-of-bounds memory access. This is a potential buffer 
  over-read vulnerability.

### 4. De Bruijn (libr/util/debruijn.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **Concretized symbolic size** (debruijn.c:51): The `calloc` call with symbolic 
  `maxlen` parameter causes concretization. The function ran until the instruction 
  limit was reached (200,000 instructions), indicating complex recursive control flow 
  in the de Bruijn sequence generation.

### 5. Base32 (libr/util/base32.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **External call with symbolic argument: toupper** (base32.c:115): The 
  `base32_decode_ut64` function calls `toupper()` with a symbolic character argument. 
  KLEE cannot model this external call with symbolic arguments, which prevents full 
  symbolic execution of the decode path.

### 6. Bitmap (libr/util/bitmap.c)

**Errors Found**: 0
- No errors found. The bitmap operations (set, unset, test, count) executed 
  successfully with symbolic bit positions. The assertions in the harness were 
  satisfied, indicating the bitmap implementation is correct for the tested 
  properties.

### 7. Bloom Filter (libr/util/bloom.c)

**Errors Found**: 2
- **Concretized symbolic size** (bloom.c:43, bloom.c:47): Both `malloc` and `calloc` 
  calls with symbolic `m` and `k` parameters cause concretization. The bloom filter 
  implementation itself appears correct - the assertion that `r_bloom_check` returns 
  true after `r_bloom_add` was satisfied.

### 8. Getopt (libr/util/getopt.c)

**Errors Found**: 1
- **External call with symbolic argument: strchr** (getopt.c:48): The `r_getopt_next` 
  function calls `strchr` with a symbolic option character. Despite this, KLEE 
  successfully explored 501 paths and generated 339 test cases, demonstrating 
  extensive coverage of the option parsing logic including various option combinations.

### 9. Random Art (libr/util/randomart.c)

**Errors Found**: 0
- No errors found. The `r_print_randomart` function executed successfully with 
  symbolic digest data and address. The assertion that the output starts with '+' 
  (the border character) was satisfied.

### Potential Memory Safety Issue in b36_tonum() (base36.c:68)

- Edge cases for boundary conditions

tool_calls.command:
# Final verification of all results
echo "=== Analysis Results Directory ==="
ls -la /analysis-results/
echo ""
echo "=== Summary of all test cases ==="
total_tests=0
total_errors=0
for dir in /analysis-results/klee-*/; do
  name=$(basename $dir)
  tests=$(ls "$dir"*.ktest 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  errors=$(ls "$dir"*.err 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
  total_tests=$((total_tests + tests))
  total_errors=$((total_errors + errors))
  echo "  $name: $tests test cases, $errors error files"
done
echo ""
echo "Total test cases: $total_tests"
echo "Total error files: $total_errors"
echo ""
echo "=== KLEE binary ==="
/workspace/klee/build/bin/klee --version 2>&1 | head -5
echo ""
echo "=== All files in analysis results ==="
find /analysis-results -type f | sort
